'''''Dictyosperma''''' is a [[monotypic]] [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[arecaceae|palm]] family found in the [[Mascarene Islands]] in the [[Indian Ocean]] ([[Mauritius]], [[Réunion]] and [[Rodrigues (island)|Rodrigues]]). The sole [[species]], '''''Dictyosperma album''''', is widely cultivated in the [[tropics]] but has been farmed to near [[extinction]] in its native habitat.<ref>[http://www.floridata.com/ref/d/dict_alb.cfm Dictyosperma album], Floridata website (accessed March 19, 2008)</ref> It is commonly called '''princess palm''' or '''hurricane palm''', the latter owing to its ability to withstand strong winds by easily shedding leaves.<ref name=riffle>Riffle, Robert L. and Craft, Paul (2003) ''An Encyclopedia of Cultivated Palms''. Portland: Timber Press. {{ISBN|0-88192-558-6}} / {{ISBN|978-0-88192-558-6}}</ref> It is closely related to, and resembles, palms in the genus ''[[Archontophoenix]]''.<ref name=riffle/> The genus is named from two [[Greek language|Greek]] words meaning "net" and "seed" and the epithet is [[Latin]] for "white", the common color of the crownshaft at the top of the trunk.

== Description ==
[[Image:Dictyosperma album fruits.JPG|thumb|140px|left|Fruit]]The ringed trunks are solitary at 15 cm in diameter with a slight bulge at the base, occasionally reaching up to 12 m in height. The [[crownshaft]] is over a meter tall, swollen at the base, and covered in white wax— which has given the palm its epithet ''album''— and small, matted brown hairs, producing a rounded leaf crown 4.5 m wide and 3 m tall. The 2.5 to 3 m [[leaf|leaves]] are borne on short 30 cm petioles; the arching leaflets are pointed at the apice, from 60 – 90 cm, dark green in color, and emerge from the rachis in a single plane.

On flowering, they produce up to six [[inflorescence]]s which ring the trunk below the crownshaft, branched to one order, with white to yellow [[flower]]s, which are [[Dioecious|male and female]]; both pistillate and staminate flowers have three sepals and three [[petal]]s, the former being smaller than the latter. The ovoid [[fruit]] ripen to purple or black in color, containing one brown, ellipsoidal [[seed]].

Three [[variety (botany)|varieties]] are currently recognized:
* ''Dictyosperma album'' var. ''album'' <small>(Bory) Scheff.</small> - [[Mauritius]], [[Réunion]]
* ''Dictyosperma album'' var. ''aureum'' <small>Balf.f. in J.G.Baker</small> - [[Rodrigues Island]]
* ''Dictyosperma album'' var. ''conjugatum'' <small>H.E.Moore & J.Guého</small> - 2 remaining specimens on [[Île Ronde, Mauritius|Île Ronde of Mauritius]] (Characterised by shorter trunk and white leaf-scar)

== Distribution and habitat ==
Living in the coastal [[forest]]s of the Mascarenes, they experience warm temperatures, high humidity and regular rainfall.<ref name=uhl>Uhl, Natalie W. and Dransfield, John (1987) ''Genera Palmarum - A classification of palms based on the work of Harold E. Moore''. Lawrence, Kansas: Allen Press. {{ISBN|0-935868-30-5}} / {{ISBN|978-0-935868-30-2}}</ref>

== ''Asterolecanium dictyospermae'' ==
''[[Asterolecanium|Asterolecanium dictyospermae]]'' is a species of sap sucking scale insect found only on Île Ronde on the two remaining ''Dictyosperma album'' var. ''conjugatum'' specimens. It apparently evolved on Île Ronde and became restricted to feeding upon the island's endemic variety, and due to interbreeding (between varieties) on Mauritius itself which jeopardized reproductive potential, the scale insect increased in population as a result of stress upon the host, which then threatens the existence of both host and scale insect.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248845438|title=A new species of Asterolecanium Targioni Tozzetti (Homoptera: Asterolecaniidae) on a palm in Round Island, Mauritius: a conservation puzzle|website=ResearchGate|language=en|access-date=2018-12-28}}</ref> <gallery class="center">
